content:
nancy_customer: Hi support, we're getting intermittent 429s and some billing alerts saying project quota exceeded even though our org-level quota should cover it. This started after we rotated keys and moved a service into a different project.

nancy_customer: Example failed response (raw):

nancy_customer: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 May 2026 09:02:14 GMT
Server: redwood-edge/1.6
x-request-id: req_02ABCD9E
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 86
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"type":"quota_exceeded","message":"Project quota exceeded"}}
```

nancy_customer: Console shows org quota usage at 30% and project A quota at 105% (weird). We have two API keys: sk-prod-A (bound to project A) and sk-org (org-level key used for shared background jobs). We rotated sk-prod-A this morning and updated the service config. Could rotation cause sudden double-counting between project and org?

ashley_support: thanks for the details. Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Are the rotated keys both valid (no duplicate strings) and not being used simultaneously by multiple services? 2) Are you proxying requests through a partner that injects an Authorization header? 3) Can you paste the SDK client version / any middleware that might clone requests?

nancy_customer: 1) Keys are unique strings. 2) We use an internal gateway that rewrites Authorization for older microservices; it sets Authorization: Bearer <key> based on route metadata. 3) SDK is python-redwood v1.3.2 with a custom retry wrapper.

diego_sre: logging note: project and org quotas are accounted at the auth layer after key validation. The usual flow: edge enforcement (ip burst) -> auth (validate key and attribute mapping to project/org) -> quota accounting. If your gateway rewrites Authorization, there's a chance requests intended for project B are being stamped with sk-prod-A or sk-org accidentally, which would attribute usage to the wrong project and potentially push that project past its limit.

nancy_customer: hmmm that could happen. We have a migration where the gateway maps service ids -> keys via a lookup table. We just deployed a change earlier today that defaulted to returning sk-prod-A when lookup misses.

quota-bot: Automated: Project A quota exceeded at 2026-05-10T09:01:58Z (project_quota=1,000,000 tokens/day, usage=1,050,123). Org quota usage 30% (org_quota=10,000,000 tokens/day). Alert SUP-6677 created.

ashley_support: likely root cause: gateway misconfiguration stamping sk-prod-A on many requests, causing project A to be over-consumed while org-level quota remains healthy. Two follow-ups: 1) Can you dump 50 recent x-request-id values from the gateway access logs and share here (we'll correlate to auth logs)? 2) Temporarily stop defaulting to sk-prod-A on misses and instead return 401 on lookup failures so you can detect misrouted traffic.

nancy_customer: we can do that. One more weird thing: a small fraction of requests show 'X-Redwood-Scope: org' header and others show 'X-Redwood-Scope: project:proj-A'. Is that header generated by the auth layer?

diego_sre: yes, auth emits X-Redwood-Scope to downstreams for debugging: values are 'project:<id>' or 'org:<id>' and help identify which quota was applied. If your gateway strips/rewrites headers or caches responses that could cause mismatch. Also note: if a request uses sk-org (org-level key) but includes a project override in the request body/metadata, we first validate key scope — org keys don't auto-attribute to projects unless your account has auto-mapping enabled.

nancy_customer: interesting — we do have a middleware that caches auth responses for 30s keyed by the Authorization header value. If the gateway stamps sk-prod-A on many paths, auth cache will speed up but also mask the misattribution.

ashley_support: recommended immediate steps:
- revert gateway default behavior so missing lookups fail (avoid stamping a specific key)
- rotate sk-prod-A and issue a short-lived sk-prod-A-temp for sessions that need it (this invalidates any accidental long-running use)
- collect x-request-id list and share with SUP-6677 so SRE can remap usage and consider a temporary quota adjustment if customer-facing errors persist

nancy_customer: will revert default and rotate key. If you rotate sk-prod-A from your side will that invalidate the key immediately? We have some long-running jobs that might break.

diego_sre: key rotation invalidates immediately. For smooth rotation: create sk-prod-A-new, deploy gateway change to prefer new key, roll traffic gradually, then revoke old sk-prod-A after verifying. If you need a safety window, create sk-prod-A-staged with narrow scope and short TTL.

deploybot: Note: system scheduled rotate for sk-prod-A at 2026-05-10T08:55:00Z completed (rotation-id rot_88aa). New key created sk-prod-A-2 (staged).

nancy_customer: aha that matches the time we started seeing quota noise. We deployed the gateway change just after that rotate. Looks like we accidentally defaulted to the old key on misses.

ashley_support: follow-up on edge cases: if multiple API keys map to the same underlying project (e.g., old and new keys both assigned to project A), quota accounting should sum usage across those keys into project A. Org-level keys are separate buckets. If you want to move consumption from project to org (for burst absorption), you can request a temporary org-level override for specific request-ids, but that's a manual SRE action and requires justification.

diego_sre: also note: IP-based protections are independent and will still trigger if a single egress IP produces a burst. For your background jobs using the org key, ensure they don't all share a single NAT IP for large fanout.

nancy_customer: action items for us: revert gateway default, rotate keys with staged rollout, collect 100 x-request-ids and paste into SUP-6677, throttle background jobs and shard across additional egress IPs.

ashley_support: I'll tag SUP-6677 with recommended temporary relief: we can apply a one-time project quota buffer (5% / two hours) to avoid user-facing 429s while you fix the gateway, but will need the request-ids and expected traffic profile.

quota-bot: Note: temporary quota buffer request logged SUP-6677-BUF. Awaiting SRE approval.

nancy_customer: sending logs now. thanks, this explains the mismatch.
